newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei ends firmer but off day's high.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei ends firmer but off day's high.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended higher on Thursday, fuelled by Wall Street's overnight gains, dealers said.
"The morning market gapped up following the Dow's surge yesterday and after that, it just continued to rise," said a dealer.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 March contract opened at 18,620 against its previous close at 18,440.
It ended 295 points up, at 18,735 after hitting a high of 18,870. Turnover was light at 23,000 lots.
After a flurry of morning activity among US and Japanese institutions, dealers said afternoon turnover was thin and mostly local-drivened.
Comments by policy chief of Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party, Taku Yamazaki, on using public funds to protect investors against debenture defaults helped underpinned the market at open.
"Yamazaki's comments were construed as positive as the market thinks the funds will be invested in the stock market," said another dealer.
Some money from the Japanese government bond market was seen diverted into the Nikkei though the amount was not significant, dealers said.
The March MSCI Taiwan stock index contract ended up 3.2 points at 318.8 against its opening 316.5 on 247 lots.
